translations.literal: Biographies 61: Loyalty and Righteousness III ○ Tushan Hang, Wanyan Chen Heshang, Yang Woyan, Wugulun Heihan, Tuoman Hutumen, Ji Ruzuo, Ai Shen, Ma Jianlong
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 61: Loyalty and Righteousness III — Tushan Hang, Wanyan Chen Heshang, Yang Woyan, Wugulun Heihan, Tuoman Hutumen, Ji Ruzuo, Ai Shen, and Ma Jianlong

translations.literal: (Supplementary)
translations.idiomatic: (Supplementary)

sentences.zh: 禹顯 張邦憲 劉全

translations.literal: Yu Xian, Zhang Bangxian, Liu Quan
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xian, Zhang Bangxian, and Liu Quan

sentences.zh: 徒單航

translations.literal: Tushan Hang
translations.idiomatic: Tushan Hang

sentences.zh: 徒單航，一名張僧，駙馬樞密使某之子也。

translations.literal: Tushan Hang, also called Zhang Seng, was the son of a certain Marshal of the Secretariat who was an imperial son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Tushan Hang, also called Zhang Seng, was the son of a certain Marshal of the Secretariat who was an imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 父號九駙馬，衛王有事北邊，改授都元帥，仍權平章，殊不允人望。

translations.literal: His father was known as the Nine Imperial Sons-in-law. When the Prince of Wei had business in the north, he was reassigned as supreme commander and concurrently acting chief councilor — far from satisfying public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: His father was known as the Nine Imperial Sons-in-law. When the Prince of Wei had business in the north, he was reassigned as supreme commander and concurrently acting chief councilor — far from satisfying public expectation.

sentences.zh: 張僧時為吏部侍郎，力勸其父請辭帥職，遂拜平章。

translations.literal: Zhang Seng was then vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and strongly urged his father to request relief from the commandership; his father was then appointed chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Seng was then vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and strongly urged his father to request relief from the commandership; his father was then appointed chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年，胡沙虎弑逆，降航為安州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhining, Hushahu committed regicide; Hang was demoted to prefect of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhining, Hushahu committed regicide; Hang was demoted to prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 會北兵大至城下，聲言「都城已失守，汝可速降。」

translations.literal: When the Northern army came in force beneath the walls, they proclaimed, "The capital has already fallen — you may surrender at once."
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern army came in force beneath the walls, they proclaimed, "The capital has already fallen — you may surrender at once."

sentences.zh: 航謂其民曰：「城守雖嚴，萬一攻破，汝輩無孑遺矣。

translations.literal: Hang said to the people, "Though the city's defense is strict, if by mischance it is breached, none of you will survive.
translations.idiomatic: Hang said to the people, "Though the city's defense is strict, if by mischance it is breached, none of you will survive.

sentences.zh: 我家兩世駙馬，受國厚恩，決不可降。

translations.literal: My family has been imperial sons-in-law for two generations and has received thick grace from the state — we absolutely cannot surrender.
translations.idiomatic: My family has been imperial sons-in-law for two generations and has received thick grace from the state — we absolutely cannot surrender.

sentences.zh: 汝輩計將安出？」

translations.literal: What do you plan to do?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you plan to do?"

sentences.zh: 其民曰：「太守不屈，我輩亦何忍降，願以死守。」

translations.literal: The people said, "If the prefect will not submit, how can we bear to surrender? We wish to defend to the death."
translations.idiomatic: The people said, "If the prefect will not submit, how can we bear to surrender? We wish to defend to the death."

sentences.zh: 航乃盡出家財以犒軍民，軍民皆盡力備禦。

translations.literal: Hang then spent all his family wealth to reward army and people, and army and people alike strove to prepare the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Hang then spent all his family wealth to reward army and people, and army and people alike strove to prepare the defense.

sentences.zh: 又五日，城危，航度不可支，謂其妻孥曰：「今事急矣，惟有死爾。」

translations.literal: Five days later the city was in peril; Hang judged it could not be held and said to his wife and children, "Matters are urgent now — there is nothing but death."
translations.idiomatic: Five days later the city was in peril; Hang judged it could not be held and said to his wife and children, "Matters are urgent now — there is nothing but death."

sentences.zh: 乃先縊其妻拏，謂其家人曰：「我死即撤屋焚之。」

translations.literal: He first strangled his wife and children, and said to his household, "When I am dead, tear down the house and burn it."
translations.idiomatic: He first strangled his wife and children, and said to his household, "When I am dead, tear down the house and burn it."

sentences.zh: 遂自縊死。

translations.literal: Then he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Then he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 城破，人猶力戰，曰：「太守既死，我輩不可獨降。」

translations.literal: When the city fell, the people still fought fiercely, saying, "The prefect is already dead — we cannot surrender alone."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the people still fought fiercely, saying, "The prefect is already dead — we cannot surrender alone."

sentences.zh: 死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were very many.

sentences.zh: 完顏陳和尚

translations.literal: Wanyan Chen Heshang
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Chen Heshang

sentences.zh: 完顏陳和尚，名彝，字良佐，亦以小字行，豐州人。

translations.literal: Wanyan Chen Heshang, personal name Yi, courtesy name Liangzuo, also commonly known by his childhood name, was a native of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Chen Heshang, personal name Yi and courtesy name Liangzuo, was also commonly known by his childhood name. He came from Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 系出蕭王諸孫。

translations.literal: He was descended from the Prince of Xiao's line of grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: He belonged to a branch descended from the Prince of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 父乞哥，泰和南征，以功授同知階州軍事，及宋複階州，乞哥戰歿于嘉陵江。

translations.literal: His father Qige, during the Taihe southern campaign, was rewarded for merit with the post of associate commissioner of Jiezhou military affairs. When the Song recovered Jiezhou, Qige died fighting on the Jialing River.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qige received the post of associate commissioner of Jiezhou military affairs for service in the Taihe southern campaign. When the Song retook Jiezhou, he was killed in battle on the Jialing River.

sentences.zh: 貞祐中，陳和尚年二十余，為北兵所掠，大帥甚愛之，置帳下。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyou period, Chen Heshang was a little over twenty when he was captured by Northern troops. The supreme commander took a great liking to him and kept him in his own camp.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyou, when Chen Heshang was in his early twenties, Northern troops captured him. Their supreme commander favored him greatly and kept him in his personal retinue.

sentences.zh: 時陳和尚母留豐州，從兄安平都尉斜烈事之甚謹。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Heshang's mother remained in Fengzhou, and his cousin Xielie, Anping Commandant, attended to her with great care.
translations.idiomatic: His mother still lived in Fengzhou, and his cousin Tuoman Xielie, commandant of Anping, looked after her diligently.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚在北歲餘，托以省母，乞還。

translations.literal: After more than a year among the Northerners, Chen Heshang pleaded that he wished to visit his mother and asked to return.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in the north, he asked leave to visit his mother and begged to be sent home.

sentences.zh: 大帥以卒監之至豐，乃與斜烈劫殺監卒。

translations.literal: The supreme commander had soldiers escort him as far as Feng, where he and Xielie ambushed and killed the escorts.
translations.idiomatic: The commander sent soldiers to escort him home. At Fengzhou he and Xielie attacked and killed the guards.

sentences.zh: 奪馬奉其母南奔，大兵覺，合騎追之，由他路得免。

translations.literal: They seized horses, helped his mother flee south, and when the Northern army discovered it and sent cavalry in pursuit, they escaped by another route.
translations.idiomatic: They seized horses, escorted his mother southward, and when the enemy realized what had happened and sent mounted pursuit, they evaded the pursuers by taking another road.

sentences.zh: 既而失馬，母老不能行，載以鹿角車，兄弟共挽，南渡河。

translations.literal: Later they lost their horses. His mother was old and could not walk, so they put her in a deer-antler cart and the brothers hauled it together as they crossed the river southward.
translations.idiomatic: They later lost their horses. Since his mother was elderly and could not walk, they loaded her into a deer-antler cart and the brothers pulled it together as they crossed the river to the south.

sentences.zh: 宣宗奇之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 斜烈以世官授都統，陳和尚試補護衛，未幾轉奉禦。

translations.literal: Xielie received the hereditary office of commander-in-chief; Chen Heshang gained appointment as a guardsman through trial service, and soon after was transferred to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie received a hereditary post as commander-in-chief by virtue of family rank. Chen Heshang entered service as a guardsman on probation and soon became a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 及斜烈行壽、泗元帥府事，奏陳和尚自隨，詔以充宣差提控，佩金符。

translations.literal: When Xielie took charge of the Shou-Si Marshal's office, he memorialized to have Chen Heshang accompany him; an edict appointed Chen imperial commissioner and controller, with a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Xielie assumed duties at the Shouzhou and Sizhou Marshal's headquarters, he asked that Chen Heshang accompany him, and an edict appointed Chen imperial commissioner and controller with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 斜烈辟太原王渥為經歷。

translations.literal: Xielie engaged Wang Wo of Taiyuan as administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie engaged Wang Wo of Taiyuan as his staff administrator.

sentences.zh: 渥字仲澤，文章論議與雷淵、李獻能相上下，故得師友之。

translations.literal: Wo, courtesy name Zhongze, ranked in literary discussion with Lei Yuan and Li Xianneng, and so won their regard as teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wo, courtesy name Zhongze, stood among Lei Yuan and Li Xianneng in power of essay and discourse, and for that reason they treated him as both teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚天資高明，雅好文史，自居禁衛日，人以秀才目之。

translations.literal: Chen Heshang was naturally brilliant and fond of literature and history; even during his days in the palace guard, people looked on him as a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Heshang was gifted and loved literature and history. Even while he served in the palace guard, people regarded him as a scholar.

sentences.zh: 至是，渥授以《孝經》、《小學》、《論語》、《春秋左氏傳》，略通其義。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Wo taught him the Classic of Filial Piety, Elementary Learning, Analects, and Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and he came to grasp their meaning in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wo now instructed him in the Classic of Filial Piety, Elementary Learning, the Analects, and Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and he gained a basic understanding of them.

sentences.zh: 軍中無事，則窗下作牛毛細字，如寒苦之士，其視世味漠然。

translations.literal: When there was nothing to do in camp, he would write tiny characters beneath the window like a poor scholar in hardship, indifferent to worldly pleasures.
translations.idiomatic: When the army had no duties, he would write tiny characters beneath the window like a scholar in straitened circumstances, utterly unmoved by the taste of worldly life.

sentences.zh: 正大二年，斜烈落帥職，例為總領，屯方城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengda, Xielie lost his command and, by precedent, became chief steward, garrisoning Fangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 2, Xielie was removed from command and, according to precedent, became chief steward stationed at Fangcheng.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚隨以往，凡兄軍中事皆預知之。

translations.literal: Chen Heshang went with him and was kept informed of all his elder brother's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Heshang accompanied him and was privy to all his older brother's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 斜烈時在病，軍中李太和者，與方城鎮防軍葛宜翁相毆，訴于陳和尚，宜翁事不直，即量笞之。

translations.literal: Xielie was ill at the time. In the army, Li Taihe and Ge Yiweng, a soldier of the Fangcheng garrison, got into a fight; Yiweng appealed to Chen Heshang. The facts were not in Yiweng's favor, so Chen measured out a beating for him.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie was ill. Li Taihe in the army and Ge Yiweng, a man of the Fangcheng garrison force, came to blows; Yiweng appealed to Chen Heshang. Since Yiweng's case had no merit, Chen ordered him beaten in proportion to the offense.

sentences.zh: 宜翁素兇悍，恥以理屈受杖，竟鬱鬱以死，留語其妻，必報陳和尚。

translations.literal: Yiweng had always been fierce and overbearing; shamed at losing on the merits and being beaten, he brooded until he died, leaving word to his wife that she must avenge him on Chen Heshang.
translations.idiomatic: Yiweng had always been brutal; ashamed to take a beating after losing on the facts, he died of brooding, leaving his wife instructions to settle accounts with Chen Heshang.

sentences.zh: 妻訟陳和尚以私忿侵官，故殺其夫，訴於台省，於近侍，積薪龍津橋南，約不得報，則自焚以謝其夫。

translations.literal: The wife accused Chen Heshang of using private resentment to exceed his authority and kill her husband. She appealed to the provincial commission and the inner service, piled firewood south of Longjin Bridge, and vowed that if she received no justice she would burn herself to answer her husband.
translations.idiomatic: She accused Chen Heshang of killing her husband out of private spite while overstepping official authority. She appealed to the provincial office and the inner court, heaped firewood south of Longjin Bridge, and pledged to burn herself if she received no redress.

sentences.zh: 以故陳和尚繫獄。

translations.literal: For this reason Chen Heshang was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Heshang was therefore imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 議者疑陳和尚，狃于禁近，倚兵閫之重，必橫恣違法，當以大辟。

translations.literal: Commentators suspected Chen Heshang, accustomed to proximity to the throne and relying on the weight of military command, of acting lawlessly and recklessly, and held that he should receive the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that Chen Heshang, used to nearness to the throne and backed by the authority of military command, must have acted wantonly and unlawfully, and should be executed.

sentences.zh: 奏上，久不能決。

translations.literal: The memorial went up, yet for a long time no decision could be made.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but no decision could be reached for a long time.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚聚書獄中讀之，凡十有八月。

translations.literal: Chen Heshang gathered books and read them in prison for altogether eighteen months.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Heshang collected books and read in prison for eighteen months in all.

sentences.zh: 明年，斜烈病癒，詔提兵而西，入朝，哀宗怪其瘦甚，問：「卿甯以方城獄未決故耶？

translations.literal: The next year Xielie recovered from his illness. An edict ordered him to lead troops west and enter court. Emperor Aizong was startled at how gaunt he was and asked, "Can it be because the Fangcheng case is still undecided?
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xielie recovered. An edict ordered him west with the army and to attend court. Emperor Aizong was shocked by how emaciated he had become and asked, "Surely this is not because the Fangcheng case still has no verdict?

sentences.zh: 卿但行，吾今赦之矣。」

translations.literal: You need only go. I will pardon him now."
translations.idiomatic: Go ahead. I am pardoning him now."

sentences.zh: 以台諫複有言，不敢赦。

translations.literal: Because the censorate spoke again, the emperor did not dare pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate raised objections again, and the emperor did not dare issue a pardon.

sentences.zh: 未幾，斜烈卒。

translations.literal: Before long, Xielie died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xielie died.

sentences.zh: 上聞，始馳赦陳和尚，曰：「有司奏汝以私忿殺人。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he at last sent an urgent pardon for Chen Heshang, saying, "The authorities report that you killed a man in private spite.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he finally issued an urgent pardon for Chen Heshang, saying, "The authorities report that you killed a man out of private resentment.

sentences.zh: 汝兄死，失吾一名將。

translations.literal: Your elder brother is dead — I have lost one of my great generals.
translations.idiomatic: Your brother is dead, and I have lost one of my great generals.

sentences.zh: 今以汝兄故，曲法赦汝，天下必有議我者。

translations.literal: Now I pardon you against the law for your elder brother's sake. There are bound to be those in the realm who will criticize me.
translations.idiomatic: For your brother's sake I am bending the law to pardon you. People throughout the realm will surely criticize me for it.

sentences.zh: 他日，汝奮發立功名，國家得汝力，始以我為不妄赦矣。」

translations.literal: Later, when you rouse yourself and win merit and renown, and the state gains strength from you, then they will know I did not pardon you lightly."
translations.idiomatic: But if you go on to win glory and merit for the state, then people will see that I did not pardon you in vain."

sentences.zh: 陳和尚且泣且拜，悲動左右，不能出一言為謝。

translations.literal: Chen Heshang wept and bowed, his grief moving those around him; he could not get out a word of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Heshang wept as he bowed, moving everyone present; he could not speak a word of thanks.

sentences.zh: 乃以白衣領紫微軍都統，逾年轉忠孝軍提控。

translations.literal: He was then appointed commander-in-chief of the Ziwei Army in plain clothes, and a year later was transferred to controller of the Loyal and Filial Army.
translations.idiomatic: He then commanded the Ziwei Army as a commoner appointee, and a year later became controller of the Loyal and Filial Army.

sentences.zh: 五年，北兵入大昌原，平章合達問誰可為前鋒者，陳和尚出應命。

translations.literal: In year five, Northern troops entered Dachangyuan. Privy Councillor Heda asked who could serve as vanguard; Chen Heshang stepped forward to answer the call.
translations.idiomatic: In year five the Northern army entered Dachangyuan. Privy Councillor Heda asked who could lead the vanguard, and Chen Heshang volunteered.

sentences.zh: 先已沐浴易衣，若將就木然者，擐甲上馬不反顧。

translations.literal: He had already bathed and changed clothes as if preparing for the coffin, donned his armor, mounted, and rode off without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: He had already bathed and changed clothes as though preparing for burial, then put on armor, mounted, and rode off without a backward glance.

sentences.zh: 是日，以四百騎破八千眾，三軍之士踴躍思戰，蓋自軍興二十年始有此捷。

translations.literal: That day with four hundred horsemen he broke eight thousand enemies. The troops throughout the three armies leaped with eagerness for battle — since the outbreak of war twenty years earlier, there had never been a victory like this.
translations.idiomatic: That day he routed eight thousand with four hundred horsemen. Soldiers across the three armies burned to fight — the first triumph of its kind in twenty years of war.

sentences.zh: 奏功第一，手詔褒諭，授定遠大將軍、平涼府判官，世襲謀克。

translations.literal: His merit was ranked first. By imperial hand he received commendation and was appointed General Who Stabilizes the Distance, judge of Pingliang Prefecture, with hereditary mouke rank.
translations.idiomatic: His achievement was ranked first. An imperial autograph praised him and appointed him General Who Stabilizes the Distance and judge of Pingliang Prefecture, with hereditary mouke status.

sentences.zh: 一日名動天下。

translations.literal: In a single day his name shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day his name resounded throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 忠孝一軍，皆回紇、乃滿、羌、渾及中原被俘避罪來歸者，鷙狠淩突，號難制。

translations.literal: The entire Loyal and Filial Army consisted of Uighurs, Naiman, Qiang, Hun, and others from the Central Plains who had been captured or fled to avoid punishment — fierce, overbearing men, known as hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: The Loyal and Filial Army was made up of Uighurs, Naiman, Qiang, Hun, and men from the Central Plains who had been captured or fled to avoid punishment — fierce and unruly, known to be difficult to command.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚禦之有方，坐作進退皆中程式，所過州邑常料所給外秋毫無犯，街曲間不復喧雜，每戰則先登陷陣，疾若風雨，諸軍倚以為重。

translations.literal: Chen Heshang disciplined them effectively; sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating all followed proper form. In towns they passed, beyond regular provisions they took not the slightest thing; the streets were no longer noisy; in every battle he charged first and broke the line, swift as wind and rain — the armies relied on him heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Heshang controlled them well: their movements in camp all followed proper drill. Wherever they passed, beyond what the district supplied they took not a hair's breadth; the streets were quiet again; in every fight he led the charge, quick as wind and rain, and the armies depended on him.

sentences.zh: 六年，有衛州之勝。

translations.literal: In year six there was the victory at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year six came the victory at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，有倒回穀之勝。

translations.literal: In year eight, the victory at Daohuigu.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight came the victory at Daohuigu.

sentences.zh: 自刑徒不四五遷為禦侮中郎將。

translations.literal: From convicted criminal to Vice Director for Defense against Insult in fewer than four or five promotions.
translations.idiomatic: In fewer than four or five promotions he had risen from convicted felon to Vice Director for Defense against Insult.

sentences.zh: 副樞移剌蒲阿無持重之略，嘗一日夜馳二百里趨小利，軍中莫敢諫止。

translations.literal: Deputy Privy Councillor Yelü Pu'a lacked a measured strategy. He would sometimes gallop two hundred li in a day and night for small gain; no one in the army dared remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Privy Councillor Yelü Pu'a had no gift for steady command. He would sometimes ride two hundred li day and night after trifling gains, and no one in the army dared stop him.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚私謂同列曰：「副樞以大將軍為剽略之事，今日得生口三百，明日得牛羊一二千，士卒喘死者則不復計。

translations.literal: Chen Heshang said privately to his peers: "The deputy privy councillor treats a great general's command like raiding and skirmishing. Today three hundred captives, tomorrow a thousand or two head of cattle and sheep — and the men who drop dead from exhaustion go uncounted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Heshang said privately to his colleagues, "The deputy privy councillor treats a grand command like petty raiding. Today three hundred captives, tomorrow a thousand or two sheep and cattle, while the soldiers who die gasping are never counted.

sentences.zh: 國家數年所積，一旦必為是人破除盡矣。」

translations.literal: What the state has built up over years, this man will destroy in a single day."
translations.idiomatic: Everything the state has accumulated over years, this man will ruin at once."

sentences.zh: 或以告蒲阿，一日，置酒會諸將飲，酒行至陳和尚，蒲阿曰：「汝曾短長我，又謂國家兵力當由我盡壞，誠有否？」

translations.literal: Someone reported this to Pu'a. One day Pu'a held a drinking gathering for the generals. When the wine reached Chen Heshang, Pu'a said, "You spoke ill of me and said the state's military power would be utterly ruined by me — is that true?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Pu'a. One day Pu'a held a banquet for the generals. When the cup came to Chen Heshang, Pu'a asked, "You criticized me behind my back and said the state's military strength would be ruined by me — is that so?"

sentences.zh: 陳和尚飲畢，徐曰「有。」

translations.literal: When Chen Heshang had finished drinking, he said slowly, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Heshang finished his drink and answered calmly, "It is."

sentences.zh: 蒲阿見其無懼容，漫為好語雲：「有過當面論，無後言也。」

translations.literal: Seeing that he showed no fear, Pu'a casually made friendly words: "If you have fault, speak it to my face; don't speak afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Pu'a, seeing he had no fear on his face, spoke casually to smooth things over: "When you have criticism, say it to my face; none of this talking afterward."

sentences.zh: 九年正月，三峰山之敗，走鈞州。

translations.literal: In the first month of year nine, after the defeat at Sanfeng Mountain, they fled to Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year nine, after the defeat at Mount Sanfeng, they fled to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 城破，大兵入，即縱軍巷戰。

translations.literal: When the city fell and Northern troops entered, they immediately let the army fight house to house in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell and the Northern army entered, they at once allowed their troops to fight through the lanes.

sentences.zh: 陳和尚趨避隱處，殺掠稍定乃出，自言曰：「我金國大將，欲見白事。」

translations.literal: Chen Heshang ran to a hiding place; when the killing and looting had quieted a little he came out and said of himself, "I am a great general of the Jin state. I wish to report something."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Heshang fled to a hiding place. When the slaughter eased slightly he emerged and declared, "I am a great general of Jin. I wish to make a report."

sentences.zh: 兵士以數騎夾之，詣行帳前。

translations.literal: Soldiers with several horsemen flanked him and took him before the commander's tent.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers escorted him with several horsemen to the commander's tent.

sentences.zh: 問其姓名，曰：「我忠孝軍總領陳和尚也。

translations.literal: Asked his name, he said, "I am Chen Heshang, chief steward of the Loyal and Filial Army.
translations.idiomatic: When asked his name, he said, "I am Chen Heshang, chief steward of the Loyal and Filial Army.

sentences.zh: 大昌原之勝者我也，衛州之勝亦我也，倒回穀之勝亦我也。

translations.literal: The victory at Dachangyuan was mine; the victory at Weizhou was also mine; the victory at Daohuigu was also mine.
translations.idiomatic: I won at Dachangyuan; I won at Weizhou; I won at Daohuigu as well.

sentences.zh: 我死亂軍中，人將謂我負國家，今日明白死，天下必有知我者。」

translations.literal: If I die obscurely among these disorderly troops, people will say I betrayed the state. Today I die clearly — there will be those in the realm who know me."
translations.idiomatic: If I die obscurely in this chaos, men will say I betrayed the state. Today I die openly, and there will be those who know me."

sentences.zh: 時欲其降，斫足脛折不為屈，豁口吻至耳，噀血而呼，至死不絕。

translations.literal: They wanted him to surrender. They hacked his shins until they broke, yet he would not yield; they split his mouth to his ear, and he spat blood and shouted until death without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: They wished him to submit. They cut his shins until they broke, yet he would not bend; they split his mouth to the ear, and he spat blood and cried out without cease until he died.

sentences.zh: 大將義之，酹以馬湩，祝曰：「好男子，他日再生，當令我得之。」

translations.literal: The commander admired his righteousness, poured mare's milk as libation, and prayed, "Good man — if you are born again, may I win you for my own."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy commander honored his loyalty, poured kumiss as libation, and prayed, "Fine fellow — should you be born again, may I have you."

sentences.zh: 時年四十一。

translations.literal: He was then forty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-one.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，詔贈鎮南軍節度使，塑像褒忠廟，勒石紀其忠烈。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, an edict posthumously enfeoffed him Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, set up his statue in the Hall of Loyal Merit, and carved stone to record his loyalty and valor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year an edict posthumously made him Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, erected his image in the Hall of Loyal Merit, and carved stone to commemorate his loyalty and valor.

sentences.zh: 斜烈名鼎，字國器，畢里海世襲猛安。

translations.literal: Xielie's personal name was Ding, courtesy name Guoqi; hereditary meng'an of Bilihai.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie, personal name Ding, courtesy name Guoqi, was hereditary meng'an of the Bilihai clan.

sentences.zh: 年二十，以善戰知名。

translations.literal: At twenty he was famous for skill in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was already renowned for prowess in war.

sentences.zh: 自壽、泗元帥轉安平都尉，鎮商州，威望甚重，敬賢下士，有古賢將之風。

translations.literal: From Shou-Si marshal he became Anping Commandant, garrisoning Shangzhou; his prestige was very great. He honored the worthy and humbled himself toward scholars, with the manner of ancient worthy generals.
translations.idiomatic: He went from the Shou-Si marshal's office to Anping Commandant, garrisoning Shangzhou, where his prestige weighed heavily. He honored the worthy, treated scholars deferentially, and had the bearing of the great generals of old.

sentences.zh: 初至商州，一日搜伏，于大竹林中得歐陽修子孫，問而知之，並其族屬鄉里三千餘人皆縱遣之。

translations.literal: When he first reached Shangzhou, one day while searching the countryside he found descendants of Ouyang Xiu in a great bamboo grove; questioning them he learned the truth, and released them along with more than three thousand members of their clan and fellow townsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after arriving at Shangzhou, while searching the countryside one day he found descendants of Ouyang Xiu in a large bamboo thicket. Once he had questioned them and understood who they were, he released them along with more than three thousand kinsmen and neighbors of their community.

sentences.zh: 楊沃衍

translations.literal: Yang Woyan
translations.idiomatic: Yang Woyan

sentences.zh: 楊沃衍，一名斡烈，賜姓兀林答，朔州靜邊官莊人，本屬唐括迪剌部族。

translations.literal: Yang Woyan, also named Walie, was granted the surname Wulin-da; he was from Jingbian Guanzhuang in Shuozhou, originally of the Tangut Dila tribal group.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Woyan, also called Walie and granted the surname Wulin-da, came from Jingbian Guanzhuang in Shuozhou and originally belonged to the Tangut Dila tribe.

sentences.zh: 少嘗為北邊屯田小吏，會大元兵入境，朝命徙唐括族內地，沃衍留不徙，率本部族願從者入保朔州南山茶杞溝，有眾數千，推沃衍為招撫使，號其溝曰府，故殘破鎮縣徒黨日集，官軍不能制。

translations.literal: In youth he had served as a minor clerk on the northern border farms. When the Great Yuan army crossed the frontier, the court ordered the Tangut tribes moved inland; Woyan stayed and did not move, leading those of his tribe willing to follow into fortified refuge in Chaqigou in the southern hills of Shuozhou. He had several thousand men, made Woyan pacification commissioner, and called the ravine a "prefecture." Ruined garrison counties sent daily gatherings of fleeing bands the government troops could not control.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he had been a minor clerk on northern frontier farms. When the armies of the Great Yuan entered the realm, the court ordered the Tangut tribes relocated inland; Woyan refused to go and led those of his tribe who would follow into fortified refuge at Chaqigou in the southern hills of Shuozhou. They numbered several thousand; they made Woyan pacification commissioner and styled the ravine a "prefecture." As ruined districts sent fugitives daily, the regular army could not contain them.

sentences.zh: 又與大兵戰，連獲小捷，及乏食，遂行剽劫。

translations.literal: They also fought the Northern army and won small victories repeatedly; when food ran short they turned to raiding.
translations.idiomatic: They fought the Northern army as well and won a series of minor victories, but when provisions ran out they took to pillaging.

sentences.zh: 官軍捕之，拒戰不下，轉走寧、隩、武、朔、甯邊諸州，民以為病。

translations.literal: When government troops pursued them they resisted and could not be subdued, roaming through Ning, Yu, Wu, Shuo, and Ningbian prefectures — a scourge to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When government forces came to capture them they fought back and could not be subdued, roaming through Ning, Yu, Wu, Shuo, and Ningbian — a plague on the populace.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣人招之，沃衍即以眾來歸。

translations.literal: The court sent men to summon them, and Woyan came in with his followers.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to summon him, and Woyan submitted with his men.

sentences.zh: 時宣宗適南遷，次淇門，聞之甚喜，遂以為武州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuanzong was moving south and had stopped at Qimen; when he heard this he was greatly pleased and appointed Woyan prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong happened to be moving the capital south and was at Qimen. Delighted at the news, he appointed Woyan prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 武州屢經殘毀，沃衍入州未幾，而大兵來攻，死戰二十七晝夜不能拔，乃退，時貞祐二年二月也。

translations.literal: Wuzhou had been ravaged repeatedly. Not long after Woyan entered the prefecture, the Northern army came to attack; after twenty-seven days and nights of deadly fighting they could not take it and withdrew — this was in the second month of Zhenyou 2.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou had been devastated again and again. Soon after Woyan took office the Northern army attacked. After twenty-seven days and nights of fierce fighting the enemy could not capture the city and withdrew — in the second month of Zhenyou 2.

sentences.zh: 既而朝廷以武州終不可守，令沃衍遷其軍民駐岢嵐州，以武州功擢為本州防禦使。

translations.literal: The court then judged Wuzhou ultimately indefensible and ordered Woyan to move troops and people to garrison at Kelan Prefecture; for his Wuzhou service he was promoted to defense commissioner of his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court then decided Wuzhou could not be held and ordered Woyan to relocate troops and civilians to Kelan Prefecture. For his defense of Wuzhou he was promoted defense commissioner of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄升岢嵐為節鎮，以沃衍為節度使，仍詔諭曰：「卿于國盡忠，累有勞績。

translations.literal: Soon Kelan was raised to a military commission, and Woyan was made military commissioner. An edict said: "You have served the state with complete loyalty and accumulated merit again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kelan was elevated to a military commission and Woyan made its commissioner. An edict addressed him: "You have been utterly loyal to the state and won merit repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 今特升三品，恩亦厚矣，其益勵忠勤，與宣撫司輯睦以安軍民。」

translations.literal: Now I have specially raised you three ranks — the favor is generous. Strive all the more in loyalty and diligence, and work in harmony with the pacification commissioner to settle troops and people."
translations.idiomatic: I have now raised you three ranks — the grace is great. Exert yourself further in loyal service, and live at peace with the pacification commissioner to secure army and people."

sentences.zh: 沃衍自奉詔即以身許國，曰：「為人不死王事而死於家，非大丈夫也。」

translations.literal: From the moment Woyan received the edict he pledged himself to the state, saying, "For a man not to die in the sovereign's service but to die at home — that is no true man."
translations.idiomatic: From the moment he received the edict Woyan pledged his life to the state, saying, "A man who does not die in the ruler's business but dies at home is no true man."

sentences.zh: 三年，奉旨屯涇、邠、隴三州，沃衍分其軍九千人為十翼五都統，親統者十之四。

translations.literal: In year three, by imperial order he garrisoned Jing, Bin, and Long prefectures. Woyan divided his nine thousand troops into ten wings and five commanders-in-chief; he personally commanded four-tenths of them.
translations.idiomatic: In year three an imperial order stationed him across Jing, Bin, and Long prefectures. Woyan divided his nine thousand troops into ten wings under five commanders-in-chief; he personally led four-tenths.

sentences.zh: 是冬，西夏四萬餘騎圍定西州，元帥右都監完顏賽不以沃衍提控軍事，率兵與夏人戰，斬首幾二千，生擒數十人，獲馬八百餘匹，器械稱是，餘悉遁去。

translations.literal: That winter, more than forty thousand Western Xia horsemen besieged Dingxi Prefecture. Marshal Right Vice Commissioner Wanyan Saibusi put Woyan in charge of military affairs and led the army against the Xia. They cut nearly two thousand heads, captured dozens alive, took more than eight hundred horses, and quantities of weapons besides; the rest fled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter more than forty thousand Xia horsemen besieged Dingxi. Marshal Right Vice Commissioner Wanyan Saibusi put Woyan in charge of operations and met the Xia in battle. They took nearly two thousand heads, dozens of captives, more than eight hundred horses, and a comparable haul of weapons; the rest escaped.

sentences.zh: 詔陝西行省視功官賞之。

translations.literal: An edict directed the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat to assess merit and reward ranks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat to review achievements and distribute rewards.

sentences.zh: 興定元年春，上以沃衍累有戰功，賜今姓。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Xingding, because Woyan had repeatedly won martial merit, the emperor granted him his present surname.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Xingding, because Woyan had repeatedly won martial merit, the emperor granted him his present surname.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遙授通遠軍節度使、兼鞏州管內觀察使。

translations.literal: Not long after, he received an honorary appointment as military commissioner of the Tongyuan Army and concurrent observation commissioner within Gong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he received an honorary appointment as military commissioner of the Tongyuan Army and concurrent observation commissioner within Gong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是冬，詔陝西行省伐宋，沃衍與元帥左都監內族白撒、通遠軍節度使溫蒂罕婁室、同知通遠軍節度使事烏古論長壽、平西軍節度副使和速嘉兀迪將兵五千出鞏州鹽川，至故城逢夏兵三百，擊走之。

translations.literal: That winter an edict ordered the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat to campaign against Song. Woyan joined Marshal Left Commissioner Inner Clan Bai Sa, Tongyuan Army Military Commissioner Wendihan Loushi, Associate Commissioner of Tongyuan Army Affairs Wugulun Changshou, and Pingxi Army Deputy Military Commissioner Hesujia Wudi in leading five thousand troops out from Yanchuan in Gong Prefecture. At Gucheng they encountered three hundred Xia troops and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: That winter an edict ordered the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat to campaign against Song. Woyan joined Marshal Left Commissioner Inner Clan Bai Sa, Tongyuan Army Military Commissioner Wendihan Loushi, Associate Commissioner of Tongyuan Army Affairs Wugulun Changshou, and Pingxi Army Deputy Military Commissioner Hesujia Wudi in leading five thousand troops out from Yanchuan in Gong Prefecture. At Gucheng they encountered three hundred Xia troops and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 又入西和州至岐山堡，遇兵六千凡三隊，遣軍分擊，逐北三十餘裏，斬首四百級，生獲十人、馬二百匹、甲仗不勝計。

translations.literal: They then entered Xihe Prefecture to Qishan Fort, encountered six thousand enemy troops in three bands, sent forces to attack separately, pursued north more than thirty li, cut four hundred heads, captured ten men alive, two hundred horses, and weapons beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: They then entered Xihe Prefecture to Qishan Fort, encountered six thousand enemy troops in three bands, sent forces to attack separately, pursued north more than thirty li, cut four hundred heads, captured ten men alive, two hundred horses, and weapons beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 尋複得散關。

translations.literal: Soon they recovered San Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they recovered San Pass.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，捷報至，上大喜，詔遷沃衍官一階，遙授知臨洮府事。

translations.literal: In the first month of year two, news of victory arrived; the emperor was greatly pleased and ordered Woyan's rank advanced one grade with an honorary appointment as prefect of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two, news of victory arrived; the emperor was greatly pleased and ordered Woyan's rank advanced one grade with an honorary appointment as prefect of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 三年，武休關之捷，沃衍功居多，詔特遷一官。

translations.literal: In year three, in the victory at Wuxiu Pass Woyan's merit was greatest; an edict specially advanced his rank one grade.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, in the victory at Wuxiu Pass Woyan's merit was greatest; an edict specially advanced his rank one grade.

sentences.zh: 元光元年正月，遙授中京留守。

translations.literal: In the first month of Yuanguang 1, he received honorary appointment as prefectural governor of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Yuanguang he received an honorary appointment as prefectural governor of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 六月，進拜元帥右監軍，仍世襲納古胡裏愛必剌謀克。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was promoted Marshal Right Vice Commissioner with hereditary mouke of Naguhulai Bila.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was promoted Marshal Right Vice Commissioner with hereditary mouke rank of the Naguhulai Bila band.

sentences.zh: 二年春，北兵遊騎數百掠延安而南，沃衍率兵追之，戰於野豬嶺，獲四人而還。

translations.literal: In spring of year two, several hundred Northern raiders plundered south from Yan'an; Woyan pursued and fought at Yezhu Ridge, capturing four men and returning.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year two several hundred Northern raiders swept south from Yan'an. Woyan pursued, fought at Wild Boar Ridge, took four captives, and returned.

sentences.zh: 俄而，兵大至，駐德安寨，複擊走之。

translations.literal: Soon a large army arrived and encamped at De'an Stockade; Woyan attacked again and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a great army arrived and camped at De'an Stockade; he attacked again and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大兵攻鳳翔還，道出保安，沃衍遣提控完顏查剌破于石樓臺，前後獲馬二百、符印數十。

translations.literal: Not long after, the Northern army attacked Fengxiang on its return and passed through Bao'an; Woyan sent Controller Wanyan Zhala to defeat them at Shilou Terrace, capturing two hundred horses and dozens of tallies and seals before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, as the Northern army attacked Fengxiang and withdrew, they passed through Bao'an. Woyan sent Controller Wanyan Zhala to defeat them at Stone Tower Terrace, taking two hundred horses and dozens of tallies and seals in all.

sentences.zh: 詔有司論賞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate rewards.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the responsible offices to assess rewards.

sentences.zh: 初，聞野豬嶺有兵，沃衍約陀滿胡土門以步軍會戰。

translations.literal: Earlier, when word came of troops at Wild Boar Ridge, Woyan had arranged with Tuoman Hutumen to join battle with infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when reports came of troops at Wild Boar Ridge, Woyan had agreed with Tuoman Hutumen to meet the enemy with infantry.

sentences.zh: 胡土門宿將，常輕沃衍，至是失期。

translations.literal: Hutumen was a veteran commander and had always looked down on Woyan; on this occasion he missed the rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Hutumen was a veteran and had always slighted Woyan; this time he failed to arrive on time.

sentences.zh: 沃衍戰還，會諸將欲斬胡土門，諸將哀請乃釋之。

translations.literal: When Woyan returned from battle he gathered the generals and wanted to execute Hutumen; the generals pleaded for him and Hutumen was released.
translations.idiomatic: When Woyan returned from battle he convened the generals and meant to behead Hutumen; the generals begged for mercy and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 時大兵聲勢益振，陝西行省檄沃衍清野，不從，曰；

translations.literal: By then the Northern army's momentum grew ever stronger. The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat ordered Woyan to scorch the earth, but he refused, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Northern army's strength was mounting daily. The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat ordered Woyan to scorch the countryside, but he refused, saying:

sentences.zh: 「我若清野，明年民何所得食？」

translations.literal: "If I scorch the earth, what will the people have to eat next year?"
translations.idiomatic: "If I strip the countryside bare, what will the people live on next year?"

sentences.zh: 遂隔大澗持勢使民畢麥事。

translations.literal: He therefore held position across a great stream and let the people finish the wheat harvest.
translations.idiomatic: He held his position across a broad stream instead and allowed the people to complete the wheat harvest.

sentences.zh: 正大二年，進拜元帥左監軍，遙領中京留守。

translations.literal: In Zhengda 2 he was promoted Marshal Left Vice Commissioner with concurrent honorary status as prefectural governor of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 2 he was promoted Marshal Left Vice Commissioner with concurrent honorary appointment as governor of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，平章合達、參政蒲阿由鄧州而西，沃衍自豐陽川遇於五朵山下，問禹山之戰如何，合達曰：「我軍雖勝，而大兵已散漫趨京師矣。」

translations.literal: In the winter of year eight, Privy Councillor Heda and Vice Councillor Pu'a came west from Dengzhou. Woyan met them from Fengyangchuan at the foot of Mount Wuduo and asked how the battle at Yushan had gone. Heda said, "Our army won, but the Northern army has already scattered and is pressing toward the capital."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year eight, Privy Councillor Heda and Vice Councillor Pu'a marched west from Dengzhou. Woyan met them from Fengyangchuan at the foot of Mount Wuduo and asked how the battle at Yushan had gone. Heda said, "Our army won, but the Northern forces have already scattered and are pressing toward the capital."

sentences.zh: 沃衍憤雲：「平章、參政蒙國厚恩，握兵柄，失事機，不能戰禦，乃縱兵深入，尚何言耶！」

translations.literal: Woyan said angrily, "The privy councillor and vice councillor have received the state's great favor and hold military power. They missed their chance, could not fight and defend, yet let their troops advance deep — what is there left to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Woyan said angrily, "The privy councillor and vice councillor enjoy the state's deepest favor and hold military power. They missed their chance, could not fight to defend the realm, yet let their troops drive deep inland — what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 三峰山之敗，沃衍走鈞州。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Sanfeng Mountain, Woyan fled to Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Mount Sanfeng, Woyan fled to Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 其部曲白留奴、呆劉勝既降，請于大帥，願入鈞招沃衍。

translations.literal: His subordinates Bailiunu and Dai Liu Sheng had already surrendered and asked the supreme commander for permission to enter Junzhou and win Woyan over.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates Bailiunu and Dai Liu Sheng had already submitted and asked the supreme commander for permission to enter Junzhou and win Woyan over.

sentences.zh: 大帥質留奴，令勝入鈞見沃衍，道大帥意，降則當授大官。

translations.literal: The supreme commander held Bailiunu as hostage and sent Sheng into Junzhou to see Woyan, conveying the commander's intent that if he surrendered he would receive a high office.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commander kept Bailiunu as hostage and sent Sheng into Junzhou to see Woyan, conveying the commander's offer that surrender would bring a high office.

sentences.zh: 沃衍善言慰撫之，使前，拔劍斫之，曰：「我起身細微，蒙國大恩，汝欲以此汙我耶！」

translations.literal: Woyan spoke kindly to comfort him, then had him come forward, drew his sword, and hacked him down, saying, "I rose from humble origins and received the state's great grace — do you mean to stain me with this?"
translations.idiomatic: Woyan spoke kindly to reassure him, then had him come forward, drew his sword, and struck him down, saying, "I rose from humble origins and received the state's great grace — do you mean to stain me with this?"

sentences.zh: 遂遺語部曲後事，望汴京拜且哭曰：「無面目見朝廷，惟有一死耳。」

translations.literal: He then left instructions to his followers regarding later affairs, turned toward Bianjing, bowed and wept, and said, "I have no face to meet the court — only death remains."
translations.idiomatic: He then gave his followers their final instructions, turned toward Bianjing, bowed and wept, and said, "I have no face left to meet the court — only death remains."

sentences.zh: 即自縊。

translations.literal: He then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 部曲舉火並所寓屋焚之，從死者十余人。

translations.literal: His followers set fire and burned the house where he had lodged; more than ten died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His followers set fire and burned the house where he had lodged; more than ten died with him.

sentences.zh: 沃衍死時年五十二。

translations.literal: Woyan was fifty-two when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Woyan was fifty-two when he died.

sentences.zh: 初，大兵破西夏，長驅而至，關輔千里皆洶洶不安，雖智者亦無如之何。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Northern army broke Western Xia and came in a long drive, the thousand li of the Guanzhong region were all in turmoil; even the wise could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Northern army broke Western Xia and swept westward, the thousand li of the Guanzhong region were all in turmoil; even the wise could do nothing about it.

sentences.zh: 沃衍與其部將劉興哥者率兵往來邠、隴間，屢戰屢勝，故大軍猝不能東下。

translations.literal: Woyan and his subordinate commander Liu Xingge led troops back and forth between Bin and Long prefectures, winning battle after battle, so the great army could not suddenly advance east.
translations.idiomatic: Woyan and his subordinate commander Liu Xingge led troops back and forth between Bin and Long prefectures, winning battle after battle, so the great army could not suddenly advance eastward.

sentences.zh: 興哥，鳳翔虢縣人，起於群盜，人呼曰「熱劉」。

translations.literal: Xingge was a man of Guo County in Fengxiang; he had risen from bandit gangs, and people called him "Hot Liu."
translations.idiomatic: Xingge came from Guo County in Fengxiang. He had risen from bandit gangs, and people called him "Hot Liu."

sentences.zh: 後於清化戰死，大兵至酹酒以吊，西州耆老語之。

translations.literal: Later he died fighting at Qinghua; when the Northern army arrived they poured wine in libation to mourn him, as the elders of the western prefectures told the story.
translations.idiomatic: He later died fighting at Qinghua. When the Northern army arrived they poured wine in libation to mourn him, as the elders of the western prefectures recounted.

sentences.zh: 至為泣下。

translations.literal: Some were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Some were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 烏古論黑漢

translations.literal: Wugulun Heihan
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Heihan

sentences.zh: 烏古論黑漢，初以親軍入仕，嘗為唐、鄧元帥府把軍官。

translations.literal: Wugulun Heihan first entered service through the imperial guard and had served as garrison officer of the Tang-Deng Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Heihan first entered service through the imperial guard and had served as garrison officer of the Tangzhou-Dengzhou Marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 天興二年，唐州刺史內族斜魯病卒，鄧州總帥府以蒲察都尉權唐州事。

translations.literal: In Tianxing 2, Xielu of the imperial clan, prefect of Tangzhou, died of illness. The Dengzhou supreme commander's office put Commandant Pucha in charge of Tangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing 2, Xielu of the imperial clan, prefect of Tangzhou, died of illness. The Dengzhou supreme commander's office put Commandant Pucha in charge of Tangzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 宋軍兩來圍唐，又唐之糧多為鄧州所取，以故乏食。

translations.literal: Song armies twice came to besiege Tangzhou, and moreover much of Tangzhou's grain had been taken by Dengzhou, so food was scarce.
translations.idiomatic: Song armies twice besieged Tangzhou, and much of Tangzhou's grain had been taken by Dengzhou, so provisions ran short.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣萬戶夾穀定住入歸德，奏請軍糧，不報。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he sent Wanhu Jiagu Dingzhu into Guide to memorialize for army grain; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he sent Wanhu Jiagu Dingzhu to Guide to memorialize for army grain; there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 七月，鎮防軍馮總領、甄改住為變，殺蒲察都尉。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Chief Steward Feng and Zhen Gaizhu of the garrison force mutinied and killed Commandant Pucha.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Chief Steward Feng and Zhen Gaizhu of the garrison force mutinied and killed Commandant Pucha.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷道梗，帥府承制以黑漢權刺史行帥府事。

translations.literal: Communications with the court were cut off; the commander's office, acting on its own authority, put Heihan in charge as acting prefect to conduct marshal's office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Communications with the court were cut off; the commander's office, acting on its own authority, put Heihan in charge as acting prefect to conduct marshal's headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 既而鎮防軍有歸宋之謀，時裕州大成山聶都統一軍五百人在州，獨不欲歸宋，與鎮防軍為敵，鎮防不能勝，棄老幼奔棗陽，宋人以故知唐之虛實。

translations.literal: Soon the garrison force plotted to go over to the Song. At that time Commander Nie of Dacheng Mountain in Yuzhou had five hundred men in the prefecture; they alone did not wish to submit to the Song and became enemies of the garrison force. The garrison could not prevail, abandoned the old and young, and fled to Zaoyang, so the Song learned the true state of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the garrison force plotted to defect to the Song. At that time Commander Nie of Dacheng Mountain in Yuzhou had five hundred men in the prefecture; they alone refused to submit to the Song and fought the garrison force. The garrison could not prevail, abandoned the old and young, and fled to Zaoyang, so the Song learned Tangzhou's true condition.

sentences.zh: 會鄧帥移剌瑗以城叛歸於宋，遺書招黑漢，黑漢殺其使者不報。

translations.literal: It happened that Dengzhou commander Yelü Yuan rebelled with the city and went over to the Song; he sent a letter to win Heihan over, but Heihan killed his envoy and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Dengzhou commander Yelü Yuan rebelled with the city and went over to the Song. He sent a letter to win Heihan over, but Heihan killed his envoy and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 宋王安撫率兵攻唐，鄂司王太尉繼至，攻益急。

translations.literal: Song Pacification Commissioner Wang led troops to attack Tangzhou; Grand Marshal Wang of E Prefecture followed, and the assault grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Song Pacification Commissioner Wang led troops to attack Tangzhou; Grand Marshal Wang of E Prefecture followed, and the assault grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 黑漢聞哀宗遷蔡，遣人求救，上命權參政兀林答胡土將兵以往。

translations.literal: Heihan heard that Emperor Aizong had moved to Cai and sent men to beg for rescue; the emperor ordered Acting Vice Councillor Wulin-da Hutu to lead troops there.
translations.idiomatic: Heihan heard that Emperor Aizong had moved to Cai and sent men to beg for rescue; the emperor ordered Acting Vice Councillor Wulin-da Hutu to lead troops there.

sentences.zh: 宋人設伏，縱其半入城，邀擊之，胡土大敗，僅存三十騎以還。

translations.literal: The Song set an ambush, let half his force enter the city, then intercepted them; Hutu was badly defeated and returned with only thirty horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The Song set an ambush, let half his force enter the city, then intercepted them. Hutu was badly defeated and returned with only thirty horsemen.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，人相食，黑漢殺其愛妾啖士，士爭殺其妻子。

translations.literal: Grain in the city was exhausted and people ate one another. Heihan killed his beloved concubine to feed the soldiers; the soldiers competed to kill their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Grain in the city ran out and people ate one another. Heihan killed his beloved concubine to feed the soldiers; the soldiers in turn killed their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 官屢聚議欲降，黑漢與聶都統執議益堅，馮總領乃私出城與王安撫會飲，約明日宋軍入城。

translations.literal: Officials repeatedly met to discuss surrender; Heihan and Commander Nie held all the more firmly to resistance. Chief Steward Feng then went out of the city privately to drink with Pacification Commissioner Wang and agreed that Song troops would enter the city the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Officials repeatedly met to discuss surrender; Heihan and Commander Nie held all the more firmly to resistance. Chief Steward Feng then went out of the city privately to drink with Pacification Commissioner Wang and agreed that Song troops would enter the city the next day.

sentences.zh: 馮歸，宋軍不得入，聶都統請馮議事，即坐中斬之。

translations.literal: When Feng returned, Song troops could not enter. Commander Nie invited Feng to discuss affairs and beheaded him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng returned, Song troops could not enter. Commander Nie invited Feng to discuss affairs and beheaded him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 及其黨皆死。

translations.literal: His followers all died as well.
translations.idiomatic: His followers all died as well.

sentences.zh: 總領趙醜兒者初與馮同謀，內不自安，開西門納宋軍。

translations.literal: Chief Steward Zhao Chou'er, who had originally plotted with Feng, felt uneasy within and opened the west gate to admit Song troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Steward Zhao Chou'er, who had originally plotted with Feng, felt uneasy within and opened the west gate to admit Song troops.

sentences.zh: 黑漢率大成山軍巷戰，自辰至午，宋軍大敗而出，殺傷無數。

translations.literal: Heihan led the Dacheng Mountain army in lane fighting from the hour of chen to the hour of wu; the Song army was badly beaten and driven out, with countless killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Heihan led the Dacheng Mountain army in street fighting from morning until midday; the Song army was badly beaten and driven out, with countless killed and wounded.

sentences.zh: 宋人城下大呼趙醜兒，約並力殺大成山軍。

translations.literal: Below the wall the Song shouted for Zhao Chou'er and agreed to join forces to kill the Dacheng Mountain army.
translations.idiomatic: Below the wall the Song shouted for Zhao Chou'er and agreed to join forces to kill the Dacheng Mountain army.

sentences.zh: 大成軍敗，宋人獲黑漢，脅使降，黑漢不屈，為所殺。

translations.literal: The Dacheng army was defeated. The Song captured Heihan and tried to force him to surrender; he would not yield and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Dacheng army was defeated. The Song captured Heihan and tried to force him to surrender; he would not yield and was killed.

sentences.zh: 其得脫走者十餘人，總領移剌望軍、女奚烈軍、醜兒走蔡州，皆得遷賞，後俱死於甲午之難。

translations.literal: A little more than ten escaped. Chief Stewards Yelü Wangjun, Nuxilie Jun, and Chou'er fled to Caizhou, all received promotions and rewards, and later all died in the disaster of Jiawu.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than ten escaped. Chief Stewards Yelü Wangjun, Nuxilie Jun, and Chou'er fled to Caizhou, all received promotions and rewards, and later all died in the disaster of Jiawu.

sentences.zh: 陀滿胡土門

translations.literal: Tuoman Hutumen
translations.idiomatic: Tuoman Hutumen

sentences.zh: 陀滿胡土門，字子秀，策論進士也。

translations.literal: Tuoman Hutumen, courtesy name Zixiu, was a policy-essay jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoman Hutumen, courtesy name Zixiu, had passed the jinshi examination in policy essays.

sentences.zh: 累官翰林待制。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Hanlin Attendant Drafting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through offices to Hanlin Attendant Drafting.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，遷知中山府。

translations.literal: In Zhenyou 2 he was transferred to administer Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2 he was transferred to administer Zhongshan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，改知臨洮府、兼本路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In year three he was changed to administer Lintao Prefecture and concurrently serve as commander-in-chief of all troops on that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was changed to administer Lintao Prefecture and concurrently serve as commander-in-chief of all troops on that circuit.

sentences.zh: 叛賊蘭州程陳僧等誘夏人入寇，圍臨洮凡半月，城中兵數千而粟且不支，眾皆危之。

translations.literal: Rebel bandits Cheng Chenseng of Lanzhou and others lured Xia troops to invade and besieged Lintao for half a month. The city had several thousand soldiers but grain would not last; everyone was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel bandits Cheng Chenseng of Lanzhou and others lured Xia troops to invade and besieged Lintao for half a month. The city had several thousand soldiers but grain would not last; everyone was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 胡土門日為開諭逆順禍福，皆自奮。

translations.literal: Every day Hutumen explained to them the blessings and disasters of loyalty and rebellion, and all roused themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Every day Hutumen explained to them the blessings and disasters of loyalty and rebellion, and all roused themselves.

sentences.zh: 因捕其黨欲為內應者二十人，斬之，擲首城外。

translations.literal: He then captured twenty of their party who meant to serve as inside collaborators, beheaded them, and threw their heads outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured twenty of their party who meant to serve as inside collaborators, beheaded them, and threw their heads outside the wall.

sentences.zh: 賊四面來攻，乃夜出襲賊壘，夏兵大亂，金軍乘之，遂大捷，夏人遁去。

translations.literal: When the bandits attacked from all four sides, he went out by night to raid their camp. Xia troops fell into great disorder; Jin forces pressed the advantage and won a great victory, and the Xia fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits attacked from all four sides, he went out by night to raid their camp. Xia troops fell into great disorder; Jin forces pressed the advantage and won a great victory, and the Xia fled.

sentences.zh: 四年，知河中府事，權河東南路宣撫副使。

translations.literal: In year four he administered Hezhong Prefecture and served as acting vice pacification commissioner of Hedong South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he administered Hezhong Prefecture and served as acting vice pacification commissioner of Hedong South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十月，進元帥右監軍、兼前職。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was promoted Marshal Right Vice Commissioner while retaining his previous posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted Marshal Right Vice Commissioner while retaining his previous posts.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，為絳陽軍節度使、兼絳州管內觀察使。

translations.literal: In Xingding 2 he became Military Commissioner of the Jiangyang Army and concurrent observation commissioner within Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 2 he became Military Commissioner of the Jiangyang Army and concurrent observation commissioner within Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十月，遷元帥左監軍、行元帥府事、兼知晉安府、河東南路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was transferred to Marshal Left Vice Commissioner, acting marshal's office affairs, concurrent administrator of Jin'an Prefecture, and commander-in-chief of Hedong South Circuit troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was transferred to Marshal Left Vice Commissioner, acting marshal's headquarters affairs, concurrent administrator of Jin'an Prefecture, and commander-in-chief of Hedong South Circuit troops.

sentences.zh: 於是，修城池，繕甲兵，積芻糧，以備戰守。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired walls and moats, maintained armor and weapons, and stockpiled fodder and grain to prepare for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he repaired walls and moats, maintained armor and weapons, and stockpiled fodder and grain to prepare for war and defense.

sentences.zh: 民不悅，行省胥鼎聞之，遺以書曰：「元帥始鎮河中，惠愛在民，移ＩＭ晉安，遠近忻仰。

translations.literal: The people were displeased. Branch Secretariat chief Xudin heard of it and sent a letter saying, "When the marshal first garrisoned Hezhong, his kindness and care rested on the people; when he moved to Jin'an, near and far rejoiced in him.
translations.idiomatic: The people were displeased. Branch Secretariat chief Xudin heard of it and sent a letter saying, "When the marshal first garrisoned Hezhong, his kindness and care rested on the people; when he moved to Jin'an, near and far rejoiced in him.

sentences.zh: 去歲兵入，平陽不守，河東保完者惟絳而已。

translations.literal: Last year when troops entered, Pingyang could not be held; of Hedong, only Jiang remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Last year when troops entered, Pingyang could not be held; of Hedong, only Jiang remained intact.

sentences.zh: 蓋公坐籌制勝，威德素著，故不動聲氣以至無虞也。

translations.literal: This was because you sat and planned to victory; your authority and virtue have long been established, so without raising an alarm you reached a state free of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: This was because you sat and planned to victory; your authority and virtue have long been established, so without raising an alarm you reached a state free of trouble.

sentences.zh: 邇來傳聞，治政太剛，科征太重，鼎切憂之。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard that your governance is too harsh and your levies too heavy — I am deeply concerned.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have heard that your governance is too harsh and your levies too heavy — I am deeply concerned.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，禦下不寬則人多懼禍，用人有疑則士不盡心。

translations.literal: The ancients said that if one is not lenient toward subordinates, many will fear disaster; if one is suspicious in employing men, officers will not give their full hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that if one is not lenient toward subordinates, many will fear disaster; if one is suspicious in employing men, officers will not give their full hearts.

sentences.zh: 況大兵在邇，鄰境已虛，小人易動，誠不可不慮也。

translations.literal: Moreover the great army is near, neighboring territory is already hollow, and petty men are easily stirred — this truly cannot be ignored.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the great army is near, neighboring territory is already hollow, and petty men are easily stirred — this truly cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 願公以謙虛待下，忠孝結人，明賞罰，平賦稅，上以分聖主宵旰之憂，下以為河東長城之托。」

translations.literal: I hope you will treat subordinates with humility, bind men with loyalty and filial duty, make rewards and punishments clear, and equalize taxes and levies — above to share the sage sovereign's sleepless anxiety, below to become Hedong's wall of defense."
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will treat subordinates with humility, bind men with loyalty and filial duty, make rewards and punishments clear, and equalize taxes and levies — above to share the sage sovereign's sleepless anxiety, below to become Hedong's wall of defense."

sentences.zh: 胡土門得書，懼民不從且或生變，乃上言：「臣本瑣材，猥膺重寄，方將治隍碑、積芻糧為捍禦之計，而小民難與慮始，以臣政令頗急，皆有怨言，遂貽行省之憂。

translations.literal: When Hutumen received the letter, he feared the people would not follow and might even rebel, and memorialized: "I am by nature a petty talent who has undeservedly received a heavy trust. I was just repairing walls and stockpiling fodder and grain for defense, but common people are hard to bring along at the start; because my orders were rather strict, there were complaints on all sides, and this caused the branch secretariat concern.
translations.idiomatic: When Hutumen received the letter, he feared the people would not follow and might even rebel, and memorialized: "I am by nature a petty talent who has undeservedly received a heavy trust. I was just repairing walls and stockpiling fodder and grain for defense, but common people are hard to bring along at the start; because my orders were rather strict, there were complaints on all sides, and this caused the branch secretariat concern.

sentences.zh: 自聞訓諭，措身無所，內自悛悔，外加寬撫，庶幾少慰眾心。

translations.literal: Since hearing this instruction I have had nowhere to put myself; inwardly I repent, outwardly I add lenient care, hoping in some measure to soothe the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Since hearing this instruction I have had nowhere to put myself; inwardly I repent, outwardly I add lenient care, hoping in some measure to soothe the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 而近以朝命分軍過河，則又喧言帥臣不益兵保守，而反助河南，將棄我也。

translations.literal: But recently, by court order troops were divided and sent across the river, and there was again loud talk that the commander would not add troops to defend but instead aid Henan — that he meant to abandon us.
translations.idiomatic: But recently, by court order troops were divided and sent across the river, and there was again loud talk that the commander would not add troops to defend but instead aid Henan — that he meant to abandon us.

sentences.zh: 人心如此，恐一旦遂生他變。

translations.literal: Hearts are like this; I fear that one day another change may suddenly arise.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts are like this; I fear that one day another change may suddenly arise.

sentences.zh: 向者李革在平陽，人不安之，而革隱忍不言，以至於敗。

translations.literal: Formerly Li Ge was at Pingyang; the people were uneasy, yet Ge endured in silence until defeat came.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Li Ge was at Pingyang; the people were uneasy, yet Ge endured in silence until defeat came.

sentences.zh: 臣實拙繆，無以服人，敢以鼎書上聞，惟朝廷圖之。」

translations.literal: I am truly clumsy and blundering and cannot win men over; I dare report Xudin's letter to the court and ask that the court consider it."
translations.idiomatic: I am truly clumsy and blundering and cannot win men over; I dare report Xudin's letter to the court and ask that the court consider it."

sentences.zh: 朝廷以鼎言，遣吏部尚書守顏閭山代之。

translations.literal: Because of Xudin's words, the court sent Minister of Personnel Shouyan Lüshan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Xudin's words, the court sent Minister of Personnel Shouyan Lüshan to replace him.

sentences.zh: 或曰，胡土門欲以計去晉安，乃大興役，恣為殺戮，務失民心，故鼎言及之。

translations.literal: Some say Hutumen wished by stratagem to leave Jin'an, so he launched great labor projects and indulged in killings, deliberately losing the people's hearts — hence Xudin's words.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Hutumen wished by stratagem to leave Jin'an, so he launched great labor projects and indulged in killings, deliberately losing the people's hearts — hence Xudin's words.

sentences.zh: 未幾，晉安失守，死者幾百萬人，遂失河東。

translations.literal: Before long Jin'an fell; those who died numbered nearly a million, and Hedong was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jin'an fell; those who died numbered nearly a million, and Hedong was lost.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，改太常卿、權簽樞密院事、知歸德府事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of year three he was changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, acting signer of Privy Council affairs, and administrator of Guide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year three he was changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, acting signer of Privy Council affairs, and administrator of Guide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元光二年二月，坐上書不實，削一官。

translations.literal: In the second month of Yuanguang 2 he was demoted one rank for submitting an untrue memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Yuanguang he was demoted one rank for submitting an untrue memorial.

sentences.zh: 正大三年七月，複為臨洮府總管。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Zhengda 3 he was again made overall commander of Lintao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhengda 3 he was again made overall commander of Lintao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，城破被執，誘之降不應，使之跪不從，以刀亂斫其膝脛，終不為屈，遂殺之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of year four the city fell and he was captured. They tried to entice him to surrender but he would not answer; they made him kneel but he would not obey; they hacked his knees and shins with blades at random, yet he would not yield, and they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year four the city fell and he was captured. They tried to entice him to surrender but he would not answer; they made him kneel but he would not obey; they hacked his knees and shins with blades at random, yet he would not yield, and they killed him.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔贈中京留守，立像褒忠廟，錄用其子孫。

translations.literal: In year five an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as prefectural governor of the Central Capital, set up his statue in the Hall of Loyal Merit, and employed his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: In year five an edict posthumously made him governor of the Central Capital, erected his image in the Hall of Loyal Merit, and employed his descendants.

sentences.zh: 其妻烏古論氏亦死節，有傳。

translations.literal: His wife, of the Wugulun clan, also died for principle; there is a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, of the Wugulun clan, also died for principle; there is a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 姬汝作

translations.literal: Ji Ruzuo
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ruzuo

sentences.zh: 姬汝作，字欽之，汝陽人，全州節度副使端修之侄孫也。

translations.literal: Ji Ruzuo, courtesy name Qinzhi, was a man of Ruyang and a grand-nephew of Duanxiu, vice military commissioner of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ruzuo, courtesy name Qinzhi, came from Ruyang and was a grand-nephew of Duanxiu, vice military commissioner of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父懋，以廕試部掾，轉尚書省令史。

translations.literal: His father Mao entered through hereditary privilege as a trial clerk in the Ministry of Rites and was transferred to clerk in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mao entered through hereditary privilege as a trial clerk in the Ministry of Rites and was transferred to clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 汝作讀書知義理，性豪宕，不拘細行，平日以才量稱。

translations.literal: Ruzuo read books and understood principle; his nature was bold and unrestrained, he did not fuss over small conduct, and in ordinary times he was known for talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzuo read books and understood principle; his nature was bold and unrestrained, he did not fuss over small conduct, and in ordinary times he was known for talent and capacity.

sentences.zh: 正大末，避兵崧山，保鄉鄰數百家，眾以長事之。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengda he fled war to Song Mountain, protected several hundred neighboring households, and the crowd treated him as elder.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengda he fled war to Song Mountain, protected several hundred neighboring households, and the crowd treated him as elder.

sentences.zh: 後徙居交牙山砦，會近侍局使烏古論四和撫諭西山，以便宜授汝作北山招撫使，佩銀符，遂遷入汝州。

translations.literal: Later he moved to Jiaoya Mountain stockade. When Inner Service Commissioner Wugulun Sihe pacified the western hills, he granted Ruzuo discretionary authority as Northern Mountain pacification commissioner with a silver tally, and Ruzuo then moved into Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he moved to Jiaoya Mountain stockade. When Inner Service Commissioner Wugulun Sihe pacified the western hills, he granted Ruzuo discretionary authority as Northern Mountain pacification commissioner with a silver tally, and Ruzuo then moved into Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，汝州殘破之後，天興元年正月，同知宣徽院事張楷授防禦使，自汴率襄、郟縣土兵百餘人入青陽垛。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Ruzhou was devastated, in the first month of Tianxing 1, Associate Director of the Palace Domestic Service Zhang Kai received appointment as defense commissioner and led more than a hundred local troops from Xiang and Jia counties from Bian into Qingyang Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Ruzhou was devastated, in the first month of Tianxing 1, Associate Director of the Palace Domestic Service Zhang Kai received appointment as defense commissioner and led more than a hundred local troops from Xiang and Jia counties from Bian into Qingyang Stockade.

sentences.zh: 時呼延實者領青陽砦事。

translations.literal: At that time Huyan Shi was in charge of Qingyang stockade affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huyan Shi was in charge of Qingyang stockade affairs.

sentences.zh: 實趙城人，本楊沃衍部曲，以戰功至寶昌軍節度使，閒居汝之西山。

translations.literal: Shi was a man of Zhaocheng, originally a follower of Yang Woyan; through battle merit he rose to Military Commissioner of the Baochang Army and lived in retirement in the western hills of Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Shi came from Zhaocheng, originally a follower of Yang Woyan; through battle merit he rose to Military Commissioner of the Baochang Army and lived in retirement in the western hills of Ru.

sentences.zh: 楷自揣不能服眾，乃以州事托實，尋往鄧州從恆山公武仙。

translations.literal: Kai judged himself unable to command the crowd, so he entrusted prefectural affairs to Shi and soon went to Dengzhou to follow Duke Hengshan Wuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Kai judged himself unable to command the crowd, so he entrusted prefectural affairs to Shi and soon went to Dengzhou to follow Duke Hengshan Wuxian.

sentences.zh: 後大元兵至，城破，殺數千人，乃許降，以張宣差者管州事。

translations.literal: Later when the Great Yuan army arrived, the city fell, several thousand were killed, and surrender was then permitted; Zhang the imperial commissioner was put in charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later when the Great Yuan army arrived, the city fell, several thousand were killed, and surrender was then permitted; Zhang the imperial commissioner was put in charge of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 三月，鈞州潰軍柳千戶者入州，張逃去，柳遂據之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Liu the thousand-commander, a routed soldier from Junzhou, entered the prefecture; Zhang fled, and Liu seized it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Liu the thousand-commander, a routed soldier from Junzhou, entered the prefecture; Zhang fled, and Liu seized it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，城複破。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the city fell again.

sentences.zh: 及汝作至，北兵雖去，但空城爾。

translations.literal: When Ruzuo arrived, although the Northern army had gone, it was only an empty city.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruzuo arrived, although the Northern army had gone, it was only an empty city.

sentences.zh: 汝作招集散亡，複立市井，北兵屢招之不從，數戰互有勝負。

translations.literal: Ruzuo gathered the scattered and lost, re-established markets and streets, repeatedly refused Northern summons to submit, and fought several times with alternating victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzuo gathered the scattered and lost, re-established markets and streets, repeatedly refused Northern summons to submit, and fought several times with alternating victory and defeat.

sentences.zh: 已而北兵複來攻，汝作親督士卒，以死拒之。

translations.literal: Before long the Northern army came to attack again; Ruzuo personally directed the soldiers and resisted to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Northern army came to attack again; Ruzuo personally directed the soldiers and resisted to the death.

sentences.zh: 兵退，間道納奏，哀宗宣諭：「此州無險固可恃，汝乃能為國用命，今授以同知汝州防禦使，便宜從事。」

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, he sent a memorial by a hidden route. Emperor Aizong announced: "This prefecture has no strong defenses to rely on, yet you were able to give your life for the state. I now appoint you associate defense commissioner of Ruzhou with discretionary authority."
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, he sent a memorial by a hidden route. Emperor Aizong announced: "This prefecture has no strong defenses to rely on, yet you were able to give your life for the state. I now appoint you associate defense commissioner of Ruzhou with discretionary authority."

sentences.zh: 是時，此州南通鄧州，西接洛陽，東則汴京，使傳所出，供億三面，傳通音耗。

translations.literal: At that time this prefecture connected south to Dengzhou, west to Luoyang, and east to Bianjing; couriers went out from it, supplies were furnished on three sides, and messages passed through.
translations.idiomatic: At that time this prefecture connected south to Dengzhou, west to Luoyang, and east to Bianjing; couriers went out from it, supplies were furnished on three sides, and messages passed through.

sentences.zh: 然呼延實在青陽為總帥，忌汝作城守之功，不能相下，州事動為所制。

translations.literal: Yet Huyan Shi at Qingyang served as supreme commander; he resented Ruzuo's merit in defending the city and could not defer to him, and prefectural affairs were constantly constrained by him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huyan Shi at Qingyang served as supreme commander; he resented Ruzuo's merit in defending the city and could not defer to him, and prefectural affairs were constantly constrained by him.

sentences.zh: 實欲遷州入山，謂他日必為大兵所破。

translations.literal: Shi wished to move the prefecture into the mountains, saying that one day it would surely be broken by the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Shi wished to move the prefecture into the mountains, saying that one day it would surely be broken by the great army.

sentences.zh: 汝作以為「倉中糧尚多，四面潰軍日至，此輩經百死，激之皆可用，朝廷倚我守此州，總帥乃欲棄之，何心哉。」
